newsitem.title: UK: Wilson cabinet tightened UK belt but not its own.
newsitem.headline: Wilson cabinet tightened UK belt but not its own.

text.p: Britain's Labour cabinet in the Sixties battled to curb wages and prices but ministers refused to set an example by taking pay cuts themselves.

The idea won a distinctly lukewarm reception when first floated around the cabinet table in 1966, according to secret documents revealed for the first time on Wednesday under Britain's stringent 30-year rule.
Prime Minister Harold Wilson's government, facing an economic crisis, had introduced a prices and wages policy designed to hold down shop prices and salary levels.

But any suggestion that the cabinet might follow suit in such austere times met with little favour and the cabinet minutes concluded: "The proposal for a voluntary reduction of ministers' salaries need not, therefore, be pursued."
